judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 4 Indicators (rank 0, same statement-type grain) in Strand 1 NUMBER, Sub-Strand 3 Fractions, but sit under different Content Standards: B4.1.3.2.3 'Provide examples of where fractions are used' under the merged comparing/adding/subtracting standard, and B4.1.3.1.1 'Generate unit fractions and locate a unit fraction ... on a number line by partitioning 0 to 1 into 8 equal parts' under B4.1.3.1 equivalent/improper fractions. Their Learning Components share only the 'fractions' token: one covers real-life contexts/examples, the other covers generating unit fractions and number-line partitioning. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements under the same BASIC 6 Content Standard 'Perform a single transformation (i.e. reflection translation) on a 2D shape' (Strand 3 Geometry and Measurement / Sub-Strand 3 Geometric Reasoning), so same statement-type grain and same canonical coordinate rank (BASIC 6, rank 2). Substantive same-rank evidence supports direction from the second SFI to the first: B6.3.3.5.1 is confined to performing and identifying images of reflection on 2D shapes in a plane (LCs: 'Perform a single transformation (i.e. reflection) on 2D shapes in a plane'; 'Identify images of a reflection of a 2D shape in a plane'), whereas B6.3.3.5.2 broadens identification of images to reflection AND translation (LCs: the shared reflection-identification LC plus 'Identify images of a translation of a 2D shape in a plane'). Proficiency in performing/identifying reflection images plausibly supports success in identifying images across the wider set of single transformations, a pair-specific extension rather than generic wording overlap; the shared reflection LC and adjacent code segments are corroborating, not the sole basis. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence excerpts are truncated (24 omitted items each) and the parent Content Standard and the second endpoint carry 'same_code_different_content' audit flags, so the code sequence alone was not treated as positive evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Content Standards (same statement grain, same rank 0) under Strand 1: NUMBER, Sub-strand 2: Number Operations. B4.1.2.2 requires describing and applying mental mathematics strategies and number properties to determine answers for basic multiplication facts to 81 and the related division facts; B4.1.2.4 requires recalling basic division facts up to 100. The strategy/number-property work on multiplication and its related division facts is substantively the derivational basis for fluent recall of division facts, and the target extends the range from facts to 81 to facts up to 100, so proficiency in the first supports success in the second. Same-rank direction is grounded in this strategy-to-recall and range-extension change rather than on shared parent, code prefix, page proximity, or token overlap alone. Evidence limitation: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (26 and 24 omitted items) and no Learning Components were supplied, so the judgment rests on the standard statements and bounded hierarchy context.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Content Standards (same statement-type grain, same coordinate rank 0), so a developmental direction would need substantive same-rank evidence that is absent here. B4.2.1.1 (Algebra / Patterns and Relationships) asks pupils to identify and describe patterns in tables and charts, explicitly 'including a multiplication chart', while B4.1.2.4 (Number / Number Operations) asks pupils to recall basic division facts up to 100. The shared multiplication-chart context provides substantive, pair-specific coherence: the chart's rows/columns encode the multiplication facts whose inverses are the division facts up to 100, so pattern work in the chart and fact recall mutually reinforce each other without either being a dependency. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same statement-type grain, same resolved Grade rank 1) under Strand 2 ALGEBRA, but in different Sub-Strands: B5.2.1.1.2 (Patterns and Relationships) requires describing a given pattern orally or in writing with mathematical language such as 'one more than or less than twice', while B5.2.3.1.1 (Variables and Equations) requires expressing a given problem as an equation with the unknown represented by a letter/variable. They cohere substantively as complementary modes of representing mathematical relationships — verbal/mathematical-language description of a relationship and symbolic equation representation of an unknown quantity — which is meaningful reinforcement across the Algebra strand. However, the shared tokens flagged by nomination ('a', 'given', 'in', 'as') are generic, the two sit under different Content Standards with no sequencing evidence, and at equal grade rank there is no substantive evidence that proficiency in one is developmentally required to support the other, so a directional buildsTowards is not warranted on this bounded evidence.
